subject: Chemistry
topic: Reducing and oxidising aldehydes and ketones
title: Reducing and Oxidising Aldehydes and Ketones
summary: Reduction is easy for both aldehydes and ketones, but in oxidation the aldehyde reacts at once and the ketone resists. The reason is one H atom.

notes.title: 07 – Reducing and Oxidising Aldehydes and Ketones

keyPoints: **NaBH₄ or LiAlH₄** reduce aldehydes to primary alcohols and ketones to secondary alcohols.
**Clemmensen** (Zn–Hg, conc. HCl) and **Wolff-Kishner** (NH₂NH₂, KOH) turn C=O into CH₂.
An aldehyde has an **H on the carbonyl carbon**, so it oxidises easily to a carboxylic acid with the same carbons.
A ketone has no such H: it needs **strong conditions**.
Ketone oxidation **breaks a C–C bond** and gives a mixture of acids with fewer carbons.

quiz.q: NaBH₄ reduces a ketone to a:
quiz.explain: The carbonyl carbon carries two carbon groups.

quiz.q: Aldehydes oxidise easily because they have:
options: an H on the carbonyl carbon
